source_access: Direct catalogue and PDF downloads returned an Incapsula challenge. The evidence below is from search-indexed text of official CityU PDF URLs, not downloaded full PDFs. Historical versions are explicitly identified.
interpretation: Deductive preparation hypotheses, not measured workload savings, grade improvements, eligibility or exemptions. Fixed contact and assessment demands remain unchanged. The strongest direct completed-source edge is used, capped at 0.35 utility units per target; no recursive or same-semester transfer.

MA1300.evidence: Course overview identifies enhanced first calculus/linear algebra, three credits; prerequisite includes specified HKDSE mathematics results.

MA2508.evidence: CILOs cover partial derivatives, multiple integrals, vector integration and mathematical modelling. Lecture allocation is 39 total hours; two shown tutorial rows list four hours each; the indexed excerpt is incomplete and is not treated as a total workload figure.

MA2509.evidence: Keyword syllabus includes propositional/predicate logic, sets, relations, counting and graphs.

MA3512.evidence: CILOs address second-order PDEs, heat/wave/Laplace equations, eigenfunction expansions and modelling. Lectures total 39 hours.

MA3515.evidence: Linear, integer and nonlinear optimization with mathematical modelling, computational methods and take-home problem work. Lectures total 39 hours; assignment hours unspecified.

GE2134.evidence: Area 1, three credits, Nil prerequisites/precursors. Rational reasoning, fallacies and creative thinking use workshops, presentations/projects, individual work and a quiz. Average lecture time two hours/week and workshop one hour/week; an individual assignment carries 20% in the indexed excerpt. Other current component weights were not recovered.

edges.reason: Partial differentiation and multivariate modelling provide preparation for PDE formulation; the PDE syllabus still introduces new methods.
Multivariate differentiation may help interpret smooth nonlinear optimization. It does not cover the full linear/integer programming or computational workload.
Practice with formal logic may help evaluate arguments. Ethical reasoning, cognitive biases, creativity, group work and writing remain distinct demands.
